## The study

Flash CA, Pasalar S, Hemmige V, Davila JA, Hallmark CJ, McNeese M, Miertschin N, Ruggerio MC, Giordano TP. Benefits of a routine opt-out HIV testing and linkage to care program for previously diagnosed patients in publicly funded emergency departments in Houston, TX. *Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes*. 2015;69 Suppl 1:S8–S15 [@flash2015rush].

Vagish Hemmige wrote the original Stata analysis and maintains this repository. Scientific decisions for this repository are made by Vagish Hemmige.

## This repository

This repository rebuilds the published analysis from a single Stata .do file into labelled R scripts run in order by `R/main.R`, as a teaching resource, and keeps the original .do file beside them with only a local folder path removed. The de-identified patient data are Harris Health System data and are not in the repository; the code finds them through the `RUSH_DATA_DIR` setting on the computer of an authorized analyst. The R code has been run only on synthetic data.

Contributions follow the rules in [`AGENTS.md`](agents.qmd); open decisions and known issues are tracked in [Issues](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-RUSH/issues).

## How this website was created

The site is built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org) from the analysis scripts themselves. Each code page imports the labelled sections of its script from `R/` and shows them with an explanation; the site never runs the analysis, so it is built without the study data.

The repository was set up with the R Analysis Workflow plugin for AI coding assistants, written by Vagish Hemmige, following the layout of [COVID-infection-control](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/COVID-infection-control). An AI assistant (Claude) translated the Stata code to R and drafted the documentation under the rules in `AGENTS.md`: it works only with code, documentation and synthetic data, never with the study data, and every change is reviewed and approved by Vagish Hemmige before it is merged.

Four documents describe the project:

-   [**Analysis plan**](analysis-plan.qmd): *what the analysis does, and why.* The published methods, following STROBE and RECORD.
-   [**Architecture**](architecture.qmd): *how the code does it.* The scripts, the order they run in, what each needs and produces, and how data flow between them.
-   [**AGENTS.md**](agents.qmd): *how people and AI assistants work on the project.*
-   [**Repository blueprint**](repository-blueprint.qmd): *the layout every project of this kind starts from.*

## The pages

-   [**Home**](../index.qmd): the study in brief, what the site does, and its status.
-   [**Clinical background**](background.qmd): opt-out testing, the HIV care continuum, and the RUSH program.
-   [**Methodological background**](methodological_background.qmd): paired binary data, McNemar's test, conditional logistic regression, interactions, comparing two eras, fixed and random person effects, and Stata-to-R equivalents.
-   [**Study design and methods**](study_methods.qmd): what this study chose and why, in plain language.
-   [**Differences from the original code**](differences.qmd): every way the R version differs from the Stata file.
-   [**Setup**](setup.qmd) and [**Functions**](functions.qmd): packages, constants and helper functions.
-   [**1. Import data**](01_import_data.qmd): reading the workbooks and numbering the categories.
-   [**2. Build long data**](02_build_long_data.qmd): two rows per patient, viral load outcomes, race groups, and the stacked eras.
-   [**3. Paired comparisons**](03_paired_comparisons.qmd): McNemar's tests and crosstabs.
-   [**4. RUSH-era models**](04_fit_rush_era_models.qmd): conditional logistic regression for the visit, by subgroup, and multivariable.
-   [**5. Comparison with the pre-RUSH era**](05_compare_eras.qmd): the era models, their subgroup versions and the random-intercept models.
-   [**Tables**](tables.qmd): the article's Tables 1 to 4 built from the data with gtsummary.
-   [**Original Stata code (2015)**](original_stata.qmd): the .do file the article's results came from.
-   [**Published results and the code behind them**](published_results.qmd): each number the article reports, the step of the code that computes it, and the article's four tables with their printed values.
-   [**Analysis plan**](analysis-plan.qmd), [**Architecture**](architecture.qmd), [**AGENTS.md**](agents.qmd) and [**Repository blueprint**](repository-blueprint.qmd): the project documents.
